editorial.headline: Veterinary Medical Equipment, at Wholesale Scale
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 46792 covers the wholesale movement of animal-health equipment, open nationally to foreign investment and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46792 is the wholesale activity behind the professional equipment used in animal health: laboratory, diagnostic and surgical equipment, alongside comparable tools for animals. Its scope is practical rather than clinical. It covers bringing those goods into Indonesia, sending them out, and distributing them through the market—the commercial infrastructure that places specialist equipment in the hands of animal-health operators.

The registration audience is correspondingly broad but clearly defined: exporters, importers and distributors. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, making it relevant both to an established distribution operation and to a business entering the supply chain at a smaller scale. The code describes the wholesale movement of equipment, not the delivery of animal-health treatment itself; that distinction keeps the commercial role of the business in focus.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership for this activity at the national level. That openness is supported by the cited PMA source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders assessing a foreign-owned vehicle, this is a meaningful point of clarity: the wholesale trade in these specialised animal-health goods is not framed here as a partially reserved activity.

Bali’s position is also more straightforward than many founders may expect. This activity is not blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium, which applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the moratorium does not block PMA registration for this code. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK—not a claim that the activity is risk-free, but a clear indication that the permanent moratorium is not the barrier here. The national openness and Bali position align: this is an activity a foreign-owned wholesale business can register in Bali today, subject to the record’s stated higher-risk classification at the Besar scale.
